burnBatch().details: Gas reads as USDC (on Arc the gas is USDC), so no price feed enters the repayment; on a chain whose gas is      another token it is that token's count read as USDC, not a price. A gas estimate made at a base fee of zero      skips the repayment's transfer and comes in about 25,000 short: send it with a limit of BATCH_GAS or more.

claimBatch((address,address,uint64,uint2.details: The one way to claim: a single line is a batch of one. Every line's own books are settled before any coin      contract is called, and the calls come in the order the head of this contract gives.

params.domains_: The domain proofs, deployed before with this contract's address and epoch length; any other is        refused (`NotWired`).
params.fetch_: The route shares' destination, deployed before naming this contract, `coinStakes_`, this USDC and        `pool_`; any other is refused (`NotWired`), as are stakes and bounties that don't name this contract and        the coins this fetch buys.
params.pool_: The UNB/USDC pool the burn buffer and the fetch swap through, for good.

eip712Domain().details: returns the fields and values that describe the domain separator used by this contract for EIP-712 signature.

poolBuy(uint256).details: The quote is the swap's minimum out, so the burn gets at least the UNB it was priced at.

CLAIM_WINDOW().notice: A voucher for epoch e can be claimed through epoch e + CLAIM_WINDOW. Kept below         WITHDRAW_DELAY so every voucher's window closes before a withdrawal requested in         its epoch can complete: claims never race the payer's exit.

COUNT_GAS().notice: The gas `CoinBounties.onCountingLine` gets for one entry and payer: about twice its most on cold storage.

NOTE_GAS().notice: The gas `CoinStakes.noteLine` gets for one line: about twice its most on cold storage, with two checks         and the deepest controller sets.

ROUTE_OVERHEAD().notice: What the route leg needs beyond the fetch's own buy allowance: the transfer, paying earlier stake and         marking the coin's price, on cold storage, with margin.

WITHDRAW_DELAY().notice: A payer's withdrawal waits this many epochs, so it cannot leave ahead of what         its agents signed (§27.1 step 5).

agentOf(address,address).notice: An agent key; spentThisEpoch is what has been claimed under the current epoch's vouchers.

authorizeAgent(address,uint256,uint64).notice: Authorises (or re-authorises) an agent key to sign vouchers against the caller's         deposit, up to `capPerEpoch` a voucher epoch. `expiry` is a block number, 0 for none.         Re-authorising clears a revocation: the payer has chosen to trust the key again.         A higher cap or later expiry applies at once; a lower cap or earlier expiry only to         vouchers for later epochs, so, as with revokeAgent, a payer cannot re-authorise its         way out of vouchers the key has already signed.

burnBatch().notice: Swaps the burn buffer for UNB through the pool and destroys the UNB (R4.6): burned, when the token can         burn, else sent to the burn address. Anyone may call it, and it runs at most once an epoch. One swap         takes at most BURN_BATCH_BPS of the pool's USDC reserve; what that leaves waits for a later epoch. The         caller is repaid from the buffer at BATCH_GAS gas at the block's base fee, plus the batch margin         (`fees.batch_margin`). A batch whose swap can't be made (no liquidity, too much price impact, a pool that         breaks its word) reverts with `Refused(why)`: nothing moves, and the epoch's batch is still to run. A         buffer no bigger than the repayment is refused (`ZeroAmount`) and waits.

burnBuffer().notice: Burn shares in USDC waiting to be swapped for UNB and burned (R4.6): each claim adds its share, and         `burnBatch` spends it, once an epoch. It is part of the USDC this contract owes.

claimBatch((address,address,uint64,uint2.notice: Claims passed receipt lines, one or many in one transaction, so a claim's write cost stays below what it         pays (§27.8). All or nothing. A voucher repeated on consecutive items is checked once. Anyone may submit;         payees are paid wherever the lines say, never to the submitter.

claimedOf(address,address,uint64).notice: Total claimed under one (payer, agent, epoch) voucher stream.

coinBounties().notice: Where each counting line's price is counted for bounties released by use (`coin.bounty-by-use`).

coinStakes().notice: Where each line is noted for checks and the latest-passed flag (`coin.check`, `rank.counted-stake`).

controllerOf(address).notice: The one controller the chain can see behind `who`: the root of the set of wallets joined to it by agent         keys, each pair of a payer and a key that signed a claimed voucher for it; `who` itself when it never         signed for another or had a key sign for it. It is the same for every wallet of the set, however the keys         ran (a key of a key, two wallets each the other's key, one key of several payers), so wallets with one         controller are one party wherever the contracts count parties (a payer's paid use, a bounty's use). Both         sides signed for each join (the grant and the voucher), and revoking or letting a key expire later doesn't         undo it: what the key did for the payer it did as the payer's.

creditEntry(bytes32,address,bytes32).notice: Credits an entry to the contributor of the earliest listing of its content shown to `listings` (R2.18),         for the site that listing names, in place of whoever held it: `listings` judges which listing is         earliest. Moving an entry to another contributor makes it live under that contributor. The contributor         already holding it keeps its entry as it was, live or delisted, so showing one of its listings never undoes         its own delisting.

delistEntry(bytes32).notice: Takes the entry out of the live set. Lines already signed for it stay claimable.

depositWithAuthorization(address,address.notice: Deposits `amount` for `to`, drawn from `from` under an EIP-3009 authorisation `from` signed with this         contract as payee (`receiveWithAuthorization`, which Arc's USDC has): no approval first, and anyone may         submit it. The authorisation's nonce is `keccak256(abi.encode(to, salt))`, so the account credited is         part of what `from` signed and no submitter can credit another; USDC refuses a nonce used twice.

dnssec().notice: The DNSSEC verifier domain proofs are checked by (R4.14): ENS's DNSSEC oracle, made by `domains`'s         constructor, with its algorithms and digests fixed and no owner left to change them. Its trust anchors,         the root's DS records, are its `anchors()`. Listings reads it to put a site's name in its one form.

domains().notice: Where domains are proven, by DNSSEC alone, and their escrow released (R4.14), and their site policy         kept (R4.17). Deployed before this contract, naming it; the only caller of `payEscrow`.

entry(bytes32).notice: An entry as a client reads it, and as the coin contracts read it (`ICoinSettlement.entry`): its credited         contributor, the site its listing names, the contributor's fee, and whether it is in the live set.

epoch().notice: The current epoch, counted in blocks (R1.28). A clock only: nothing is posted per epoch.

epochBlocks().notice: One epoch, in this chain's blocks: 24 hours of them, set at deploy (R1.28). Blocks, never timestamps: a         proposer can skew a block's timestamp, and with it every delay an epoch times, without blocks passing.

feeOf(address).notice: Each node's detail fee in USDC: one price for every entry it contributes.

fetch().notice: Where each line's route share goes (`coin.fetch-pays`, `coin.fetch-buys`, `coin.split`).

heldRoute().notice: Route shares whose call into `fetch` failed, waiting here to be sent on (`sendHeld`), in all. Part of the         USDC this contract owes.

lineLeaf((uint256,bytes32,uint256,bool,a.notice: The Merkle leaf for a receipt line (OpenZeppelin double hash).

linked(address,address).notice: Whether `agent` is `payer`'s party now (R1.3): a key the payer granted, not revoked or expired, that has         signed a voucher of the payer's that was claimed. A grant needs nothing of the key, so a grant alone links         nobody; and a revoked or expired key is linked no more.

listings().notice: Where listings shown at first claim are checked and credited (R2.14 to R2.18). Made by this contract's         constructor; the only caller of `creditEntry`.

nextBurnEpoch().notice: The first epoch `burnBatch` may swap in: the last batch's epoch plus one, so zero means none yet.

payEscrow(bytes32,address,uint256).notice: Pays `amount` of a domain's escrow to `to`, only for `domains`, which judges the proof and the wait         (`Domains.releaseEscrow`, R4.14).

pool().notice: The UNB/USDC pool the burn buffer swaps through (R9.27), the one `CoinFetch` buys through, fixed at         construction like every other address here (R10.3). Its pair is this contract's own USDC and UNB.

poolBuy(uint256).notice: Buys UNB with at most `usdcMax` of this contract's USDC, and at most BURN_BATCH_BPS of the pool's USDC,         and returns what was sold and bought. Callable only by this contract (`burnBatch`), so that a swap that         fails for any reason (the pool reverts, takes the wrong amount, pays under its quote) unwinds whole.

postRoot(bytes32).notice: Posts the Merkle root of a batch of listing hashes (protocol R2.17). Anyone may,         at any time, with no bond: a root only proves that each listing under it existed         by the block it was first posted in, so posting one costs others nothing. A root         posted again keeps its first block: a later post can't move a listing's priority.         The poster publishes the leaf list off chain, beside the listings.

relistEntry(bytes32).notice: Puts the caller's own entry back in the live set after it delisted it (R2.16: republishing restores a         withdrawn listing). An entry is first listed by the claim that shows its signed listing (`listings`);         nothing else writes one.

requestWithdraw(uint256).notice: Asks to withdraw. Adds to any pending amount and restarts the delay, so every         pending unit waits the full two epochs after its last request.

revokeAgent(address).notice: Revokes an agent key from the next epoch on. Vouchers for this epoch and earlier         stay claimable within their window, so a payer cannot revoke its way out of uses         it already signed for; nothing the key signs for a later epoch is honoured. A key         stolen mid-epoch can still spend up to its cap for the rest of this epoch.

revokedAt(address,address).notice: The first voucher epoch refused after revocation, stored as the revoking epoch + 1;         0 means never revoked.

rootBlock(bytes32).notice: The block a listing root was first posted in; zero when it never was.

routeHeld(bytes32).notice: keccak256(entryId, payer) => the route shares of that entry and payer waiting here (`sendHeld`).

sendHeld(bytes32,address).notice: Sends on the route shares of `entryId` and `payer` that waited here because their call failed inside a         claim. Anyone may; it reverts whole, and they go on waiting, if the call still fails.

sendRoute(bytes32,address,uint256).notice: Sends `usdc` of route share to `fetch` and has it pay and buy for `entryId` and `payer`, as one unit that         fails whole. Callable only by this contract.

setFee(uint256).notice: Sets the caller's detail fee in USDC, for every entry it contributes at once.         Vouchers carry their own amounts; this is the published price clients charge at.

spendable(address).notice: The deposit net of pending withdrawals: what a line can be drawn on.

termsFor(address,address,uint64).notice: The terms a voucher for `epoch_` is judged by: the key's current ones, or those it         held for that epoch before a re-authorisation lowered them, whichever is more generous.

unb().notice: UNB, which the burn buffer buys and burns (R4.6).

usdc().notice: The fee currency: USDC (spec §41). Deposits, claims and the split settle in it.

voucherDigest((address,address,uint64,ui.notice: The EIP-712 digest the agent signs, for off-chain code to check its hashing.

withdraw().notice: Pays out what is pending. Claims made meanwhile may have drawn the balance         below it; then only what is left goes.
